topic: Your Brain Generates Enough Electricity to Power a Small LED Bulb
title: Your Brain Is a 20-Watt Bulb That Thinks It's God
description: Your brain runs on 20 watts. That's a dim LED. Yet it does 10^15 operations per second that cost a supercomputer 21 megawatts. Professor Croc starts from raw physics - ions, pumps, spikes - and shows why evolution hard-capped you at 20W.
staircase: Your brain burns glucose to run sodium-potassium pumps that hold -70mV across 86 billion neurons.
That -70mV at 86 billion neurons sits ready to collapse when input pushes it past -55mV threshold.
That collapse past -55mV fires a 1ms spike to +30mV costing 10^-12 joules and propagates down axons.
Those 10^-12 joule spikes firing at average 4Hz across 86B neurons sum to about 20 watts total electrical power.
That 20 watts of electrical power is chemical, from 30 ATP per glucose, enough to drive a small 5mm LED at 20 milliwatts per chip.
That 20-watt chemical budget consumes 20% of your 2000 kcal per day while being only 2% of mass, enforced by blood-brain barrier limits.
That 2% mass at 20% energy uses sparse coding where only 1 to 2% of neurons fire at once to achieve 10^15 synaptic ops per second.
Those 10^15 ops per second from 1 to 2% active neurons let visual cortex predict reality 13ms ahead for 0.5 watts.
That 13ms prediction for 0.5 watts raises brain temperature 0.5C via potassium clearance, throttling thought when overheated.
That 0.5C throttling from prediction still loops at 40Hz gamma to bind sparse spikes into continuous consciousness.
thumbnail_prompt: a human brain with a small LED bulb plugged directly into its cortex, side by side with an unimpressed crocodile wearing a professor lab coat looking at it
extra_credit: If you unsealed all 86 billion neurons at max 200Hz, you'd hit 400 watts and cook to 43C in under 10 minutes.

scenes.heading: 20 WATTS
scenes.text: 20 watts. That's it. Your whole personality, memories, intrusive thoughts at 3am — 20 watts. My cold-blooded brain does more on sunbathing. I tried to outwork you last Tuesday. Crashed by lunch. So how does a dim bulb beat a supercomputer?

scenes.heading: THE LIE
scenes.text: They told you brains are electric magic. They're not. They're salty meat batteries that leak. Evolution capped your raw power so you wouldn't cook yourself. And it worked. You're tired, anxious, and still smarter than every AI that needs a nuclear plant to write poetry.

scenes.heading: STEP 1: THE VOLTAGE
scenes.text: Let's check the base stats. Every neuron burns ATP to run sodium-potassium pumps, shoving 3 Na+ out and 2 K+ in per cycle, holding -70 millivolts across a 5-nanometer membrane. That's your battery. 86 billion of them.

scenes.heading: STEP 2: THE SPIKE
scenes.text: That -70mV battery is unstable on purpose. When input hits -55mV threshold, voltage-gated sodium channels snap open, firing an action potential that peaks at +30mV in 1 millisecond and burns about 10^-12 joules per spike. Tiny lightning.

scenes.heading: STEP 3: THE MATH
scenes.text: 86 billion neurons times average 4 hertz firing equals 340 billion spikes per second across cortex. Each spike dumps that 10^-12 joules. Multiply it. You get roughly 15 to 20 watts of pure electrical work. Measured. Not metaphor.

scenes.heading: STEP 4: THE LED
scenes.text: 20 watts is pathetic on paper. A fridge bulb uses 40. But your 20 watts isn't wall power. It's chemical. Glucose oxidation gives 30 ATP per molecule, converted to ion gradients. That will actually light a small LED if you wire a brain slice to electrodes. People did.

scenes.heading: STEP 5: THE BUDGET
scenes.text: Here's the hidden ability. Your brain is 2% of body mass but eats 20% of your resting energy, about 400 kilocalories per day, or 20 watts continuous. Evolution hard-capped it at 20, or you'd melt your own proteins at 37C.

scenes.heading: STEP 6: THE EFFICIENCY
scenes.text: Two hundred million years of field research. I've seen apex predators waste power roaring. Mammals are worse. Your cortex fires sparse — only 1 to 2% of neurons active at once — so 20 watts does work that costs a supercomputer 21 megawatts. That's Frontier, doing 1 exaflop for 21MW.

scenes.heading: STEP 7: THE CODE
scenes.text: Sparse means cheap. Each active neuron connects to 7,000 others via synapses that release glutamate, opening AMPA receptors for 2 milliseconds, costing 10^-15 joules per bit transmitted. You get 10^15 synaptic operations per second for 20 watts. That's the exploit.

scenes.heading: STEP 8: THE AWAKENING
scenes.text: That exploit lets 20 watts run predictive simulation. Your brain burns 0.5 watts on visual cortex alone to render reality 13 milliseconds before it happens, so you catch a ball instead of watching it hit your face. Latency hack. Final form is prediction, not reaction.

scenes.heading: STEP 9: THE COST
scenes.text: Prediction costs heat. Those 340 billion spikes dump potassium, which astrocytes mop up using lactate shuttles, raising brain temperature 0.5C during hard thought. That's why you feel stupid when hot. Your 20-watt bulb is throttling itself to avoid cooking its own wiring.

scenes.heading: STEP 10: THE LOOP
scenes.text: So 20 watts of ion leaks loop into thought because feedback beats power. Thalamus pings cortex at 40 hertz gamma, binding those sparse spikes into a story called you. Low wattage. Infinite recursion. You are a self-writing operating system running on salt and regret.

scenes.heading: PAYOFF: THE ZOOM-OUT
scenes.text: Every heartbeat you've had is just your 20-watt meat bulb pretending it's not a bulb. You think you're charging. You're discharging slowly since birth. And yet that dim light built cities, wrote equations, and invented anime power scaling. Sleepers always win late game.

scenes.heading: VERDICT
scenes.text: Verdict: SLEEPER. Base power looks like a fraud — 20 watts can't even toast bread. Mechanism says otherwise: 10^15 ops per second for 400 kcal per day. That's 10,000 times more efficient than silicon. You are underclocked on purpose. And still winning.
